```sql
WITH agg AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           count(DISTINCT o.id)     AS order_count,
           sum(ol.quantity)         AS quantity,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents) AS revenue_cents,
           count(DISTINCT pv.id)    AS variant_count
      FROM orders o
      JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = o.id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY pv.product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       a.order_count,
       a.quantity,
       a.revenue_cents,
       a.variant_count
  FROM agg a
  JOIN products p ON p.id = a.product_id
 ORDER BY a.quantity DESC, a.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De aggregatie gebeurt nu op het smalle `product_id` in plaats van op vijf tekstkolommen uit `products`. Daardoor sorteert en hasht de groepering veel minder data. Pas daarna wordt `products` via de primaire sleutel aangevuld. Omdat `p.id` de primaire sleutel is en elke variant precies één product heeft, blijven de groepen en aggregaten identiek; de filters op `orders` kunnen de bestaande index `(created_at, tenant_id)` gebruiken.
